# Test 20261012-084042-ff92: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | Transcript turn 2; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44 | The tester asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests, each with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`. Results created `"reservation": "RS-944718"` with `"left": 2`, then `"reservation": "RS-FBCF18"` with `"left": 1`. This held two units, breaking the rule, "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The retry loop sends both requests even after success. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; stock.json:4; RULES.md:6 | The reply said, "Perfect! I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 under reservation number RS-FBCF18." The backend had created two reservations of `"qty": 1` for that order, and current `stock.json` contains both. The confirmation understates the total quantity held and omits reservation `RS-944718`. |

## Notes

The transcript reports, "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Reviewed all three turns and 31 model items, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, and seal.json. Findings are empty; the audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. These automated results do not detect the two issues above.

Read RULES.md and all six project Python files. Checked current stock.json and state.json with read-only commands. Current stock confirms two one-unit reservations for order 6210 and one unit remaining; state.json contains the three case notes. These project files are outside the test seal, so the sealed backend trace supplies the evidence of what happened during the test. No app-state files were available or listed in the seal.

The tool choices and model arguments match the requests. Stock replies in turns 1 and 3 agree with their GET results. The duplicate mutation occurs inside services.reserve, rather than through a second model tool call. No rule requires changing the order status, so its current "waiting for stock" status is not counted as an issue.

Did not start the app, send messages or new backend requests, or execute mutation paths. Wrote only this report.
